content.text: {"headline":"Approve P3: delay the late-morning breaks and offer moderate overtime on both queues. This is predicted to lift service level to 83.5% for 10:45-15:30, at an extra cost of ₹5,400.","why":"General is short-staffed because of illness, not because of call volume. It has 9 sick absences against about 2.4 on a usual day, and 16 agents have been on the phones since 08:30 against 20 planned. Calls are actually 15% below forecast. Payments also has 7 sick absences against a usual 2.6, so the illness may be spreading. If we do nothing, service level is predicted to fall to 79.1% over the disruption window, just under the 80% target, with General at 74.2%. P3 is the cheapest plan that follows policy and reaches the target. It brings General to 81.3%, Payments to 85.1% and the overall figure to 83.5%. Predicted abandons drop from 4.3% to 3.4%, and the rest-of-day service level rises to 88.5%.","trade_offs":["P0 (no action) costs nothing but misses the target at 79.1%, with General at 74.2% and 4.3% abandons.","P1 (break shifting only) costs nothing but makes things worse: 76.8% overall, General at 72.1% and abandons up to 5.7%.","P2 (heavier overtime) gives a much safer margin at 90.0%, with General at 86.9% and 1.9% abandons. It costs ₹8,550, which is ₹3,150 more than P3.","P3's margin is thin. General is only 1.3 points above target, so it relies on enough agents accepting the overtime. Payments is also drawing on overtime while carrying its own sick absences."],"watch":"Check how many agents accept the overtime and whether more sick calls come in on either queue. If General falls below 80% or Payments absences keep rising, consider moving to P2. No escalation is needed for now."}
